question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

Giving Astha a make-over was __a piece of cake__ because she’s so naturally beautiful.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. "A task easily accomplished".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"a piece of cake"** means something that is very easy to do or accomplish. (बहुत आसान)

 
 
• **Example:** Solving that puzzle was a piece of cake for him.
 
 
 
• **"A task easily accomplished"** refers to something that requires little effort or is straightforward to perform. (आसानी से किया जाने वाला कार्य)
 
 
• **Example:** Painting the walls was a task easily accomplished with the right tools.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom "a piece of cake" aligns directly with the meaning "A task easily accomplished".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: A slice of pizza** (पिज़ा का टुकड़ा): This option refers to food and has no connection to the idiom's meaning.

 
 
• **Example:** He ordered a slice of pizza for lunch.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: A piece of pie** (पाई का टुकड़ा): This option is similar in phrase structure but does not convey the same meaning as the idiom.
 
 
• **Example:** She offered me a piece of pie after dinner.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: A piece of bread** (ब्रेड का टुकड़ा): This option also refers to food and does not fit the idiom's meaning.
 
 
• **Example:** He ate a piece of bread with butter for breakfast.
